evidence: Red run: `11 failed, 13 passed, 4 deselected in 6.60s` (.gov-runtime/scratch/lead/log/red-1.txt, red-1.xml). `gov links --since 8107e7b69`: "gov links: 0 new since 8107e7b69, 1711 standing (...)". td-1 says it got 28 passed against its own throwaway I1-I4 code in scratch, so the cases can go green. I did not re-run that.
tests: All runs went through heavy_slot.sh with TMPDIR=/tmp/w2-154-lead. The plugin file has 5 red cases: the exit-4 refusal of an entry the opt-in list leaves out, and the missing `not_in_this_run` record. It has 6 green guards: F1's exit 4 twice, an entry with one case kept, and S2's opt-in three times. The 6 nightly cases are all red because `NIGHTLY_SERIAL_STUB` is ignored today: the run stops at the secrets switch with exit 2. test_serial.py: 7 passed. None of the red cases fails on an import, name or syntax error in the tests.
discoveries:
- `gov context DAEO-l4gf` refuses with CONTEXT_OVER_CEILING (7401 tokens against the 6000 ceiling), and `--brief` refuses too. `--budget 9000` works.
- `gov accept W2-154` refuses with ACCEPT_NO_MAP: tests/unit/close/ has no README map, and a README there is outside allowed_paths. The same thing happened on W2-177, so the acceptance is these named files, run by path.
- td-1 found that pytest itself ends exit 5 when every given case is deselected. Meeting I2's "ends exit 0" therefore needs the plugin to change the exit status.
- The tests read the close's record through the private `command._run_tests(..., stated=...)`. The engineer must keep its signature and `stated` form.
risks:
- The nightly harness rewrites nightly.sh's `ORCH=`, `REPO=`, `RUNS=`, `JUNIT=`, `PING=` and `  window_end=` lines, and asserts there is exactly one of each. An engineer who changes those lines breaks the harness. Every path is under tmp_path, and the stub's CLONE never matches the real clone-removal pattern, so no real nightly state is touched.
- One F1 case needs the exit-4 message to name only the entry that names no case (B), not also an entry the opt-in list leaves out (A).
lessons: A ticket whose acceptance path is under tests/unit/<x>/ and has no README in its allowed_paths cannot use `gov accept`. A ticket that sets the path should include a README there, or name a by-path check.
proposed_decisions: none
unresolved:
- S4 conflicts with F3: the S4 restore must write tests/acceptance/serial-only.txt, which is not in allowed_paths, and F3 fails on any change outside them. This needs the CTO before the build run's S4 step: widen allowed_paths by that one file, or land S4 as a separate test-designer commit outside this ticket's diff check.
- td-1's open questions, answered from I3 for the engineer: "final line reads red" is the last `verdict:` line of run.txt plus the P1 ping. Whether the stub run still does the night-window and quiet checks is not stated, and the harness works either way.
recommended_next_action: Start run kind build: an engineer on I1-I4 against tests/unit/close/test_serial_w2_154_*.py and test_serial.py. Before the S4 step, the CTO decides S4's path.
